rationale_overall: This week's pool was overwhelmingly noise relative to the profile's wave thesis: state-actor satellite launches (China), foreign junior-miner uranium press releases (Bannerman/Namibia, F3 Uranium/TSXV, Lotus/Malawi, Leviathan Gold/Botswana) with no liquid US listing, private-company milestones with no public equity (SpaceX Starship/Starlink tests, OpenAI revenue-share reports), routine geopolitical friction with no investable ticker attached (Houthi drone strike on a Qatari/Israeli airport, Taiwan-strait warship transits, North Korean missile-engine tests), and consumer-product launches unrelated to any named wave (Garmin Fenix 8 Pro, Google Pixel Watch satellite SOS). The one plausible nuclear catalyst - GE Vernova (GEV) accelerating SMR/BWRX-300 reactor delivery timelines - was screened out because GEV's core business also includes a large offshore/onshore wind-turbine segment, which conflicts with the profile's wind-energy exclusion; a diversified vehicle that materially monetizes an excluded sub-sector isn't a clean add. Northrop Grumman's ISS cargo launch was routine resupply, not a fresh catalyst, and Alphabet/Nvidia AI coverage only reinforces theses already reflected in held AAPL/GOOGL/NVDA. Nothing cleared the bar of a clearly stronger rising-wave vehicle versus a current holding, so the watchlist is unchanged this week.
